newsitem.title: USA: Destron microchip implant approved by FDA.
newsitem.headline: Destron microchip implant approved by FDA.

text.p: Destron Fearing Corp said Monday it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to implant its microchip in cattle and horses.
The company said it has filed with the U.S. Department of Agriculture for concurrence.
"We consider this FDA approval a significant milestone in our quest to create a market for implantable identification in the livestock industry," Randolph Geissler, president, said in a statement.
Destron's microchip transponders provide a way to identify animals for purposes of disease control and automated recordkeeping.
Geissler said the company expects a decision from the USDA this year.

"This will clear the way for increased use of microchips in control programs for diseases such as equine infectious anemia, and it will also enable us to begin actively promoting our system to the beef industry," Geissler said.
